name: House of Jagiellon

Crown of Poland and Grand Duchy of Lithuania (1450-1569)

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Poland
predecessors.text: the Crown of Poland, in personal union with Lithuania under Casimir IV (King from 1447)

predecessors.name: Grand Duchy of Lithuania
predecessors.text: the Grand Duchy, ruled by Casimir IV (Grand Duke since 1440)

successors.name: Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth
successors.text: the whole realm: the Union of Lublin of 1 July 1569 merges the Crown and the Grand Duchy into the Commonwealth

rulers.name: Casimir IV Jagiellon
rulers.title: King of Poland (1447-1492) and Grand Duke of Lithuania (1440-1492)

rulers.name: John I Albert / Alexander
rulers.title: John I Albert King of Poland 1492-1501; Alexander Grand Duke of Lithuania 1492-1506

rulers.name: Alexander Jagiellon
rulers.title: King of Poland from 1501, Grand Duke of Lithuania since 1492

ledger.x: 1450: Poland and Lithuania are drawn as one Jagiellonian realm.
1450: the Crown of Poland is drawn inside the Jagiellonian realm.
1450: the Grand Duchy of Lithuania is drawn inside the Jagiellonian realm; the two states stay distinct until the Union of Lublin of 1569.
1450: the Masovian duchies are Polish fiefs.
1450: Moldavia is a vassal of the Polish crown, a status already in force when the realm begins.
March 1454: the Thirteen Years' War begins over Prussia.
1457: Casimir IV buys the Duchy of Oświęcim.
October 1466: the Second Peace of Thorn ends the war.
October 1466: Pomerelia and western Prussia become Polish.
October 1466: the Prince-Bishopric of Warmia comes under the Polish crown; the Kingdom of Poland page calls it 'a protectorate of Kingdom of Poland' to 1772.
October 1466: the Order becomes the Polish king's vassal.
August 1492: Ivan III invades Lithuania.

1494: Jan V, the last of the Zator brothers and its sole ruler in 1494, decides 'in the same year to sell the duchy to King John I Albert of Poland', with a guarantee that he remain duke until his death; 'Jan was killed in 1513 and Zator was united with Poland', and the Sejm of 1564…
5 February 1494: the 'eternal' peace ends the first Muscovite-Lithuanian war.
5 February 1494: Lithuania gives up Vyazma and the upper Oka to Moscow.
1497: the end year of the page's heading 'Principality of Moldavia (1387–1497)'; the section does not say how the vassalage ended.
1500: the second war with Moscow.
25 March 1503: a six-year truce ends the war.
25 March 1503: Lithuania loses about a third of its land to Moscow.
1503: Gomel is Muscovite when the war of 1500-1503 ends.
1503: the part of Cliopatria's 1507 loss that Moscow does not hold, the steppe east of the Dnieper.
December 1512: Moscow invades again.
July 1514: Smolensk falls to Moscow and is never returned.
1522: a five-year truce 'for Russia to retain control of Smolensk' ends the war; it was later extended to 1534.
April 1525: the Order's rule in Prussia ends.
10 April 1525: Albert pays the Prussian Homage at Kraków.
1526: the Duchy of Masovia ends.
1534: war over the Chernigov-Starodub border.
1535: Lithuanian and Polish forces retake Gomel.
1537: a five-year truce without prisoner exchange ends the war.
June 1559: Livonia comes under Polish-Lithuanian protection.
28 November 1561: the protectorate over Livonia ends with annexation.
28 November 1561: Lithuania takes the Order's land in Livonia.
1562: the Duchy of Courland and Semigallia begins 'as a vassal state of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania', under Gotthard Kettler, the Order's last master and first Duke of Courland.
1 July 1569: the Grand Duchy becomes part of the Commonwealth, whose joint sovereignty takes over the Livonian lands; Courland and Semigallia stays a vassal duchy of the Commonwealth.

1569: the suzerainty over the Duchy of Prussia passes to the Commonwealth; on 19 July 1569 at Lublin Albert Frederick paid homage to Sigismund II Augustus, and the Polish fief lasted to the Treaty of Bromberg (1657).
1 July 1569: the Union of Lublin merges Poland and Lithuania.
1 July 1569: the Jagiellonian union ends in the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.

wars.name: Thirteen Years' War
wars.outcome: The Second Peace of Thorn (October 1466) gave Poland western Prussia as Royal Prussia, Pomerelia and the Bishopric of Warmia; eastern Prussia stayed with the Order as a vassal of the Polish king.

wars.name: Muscovite-Lithuanian War (1487-1494)
wars.outcome: Moscow took the Principality of Vyazma and a region on the upper Oka; 'eternal' peace of 5 February 1494.

wars.name: Muscovite-Lithuanian War (1500-1503)
wars.outcome: Lithuanian defeats at Vedrosha (14 July 1500) and Mstislavl (November 1501); the truce of 25 March 1503 gave Moscow about 210,000 km2 including Chernigov, Novgorod-Seversk and Starodub.

wars.name: Muscovite-Lithuanian War (1507-1508)
wars.outcome: Sigismund I asked for the return of the 1503 gains; Glinski's rebellion ran alongside; the 'eternal peace' of 8 October 1508 kept the accords of the 1503 truce.

wars.name: Muscovite-Lithuanian War (1512-1522)
wars.outcome: Smolensk fell in July 1514 and was kept by Moscow under the five-year truce of 1522; Lithuania won at Orsha on 8 September 1514 but lost about 56,000 km2.

wars.name: Polish-Teutonic War (1519-1521)
wars.outcome: The Polish General Sejm declared war in December 1519 and fighting began in January 1520; the armistice of Thorn of 5 April 1521 ended it; the Treaty of Kraków of 1525 secularised the Order's state as the Duchy of Prussia, a Polish fief.

wars.name: Muscovite-Lithuanian War (1534-1537)
wars.outcome: Lithuanian and Polish forces took Gomel and Starodub; the five-year truce left Homel to the king while Moscow kept Sebezh and Zavoloche; Starodub is not named in the truce.

wars.name: Polish-Moldavian campaign of John I Albert (1497)
wars.outcome: The siege of Suceava (24 September to 19 October 1497) failed and the Poles were defeated in the Cosmin Forest (26 October 1497, the text says the battle began on the night of 25 October); Poland sued for peace in 1499.

wars.name: Livonian War

certainty.note: The level is the realm-wide minimum: the Muscovite, Tatar and steppe frontiers are approximate, and the Teutonic frontier in Prussia is drawn from Cliopatria's outline, not from a treaty line, until the Second Peace of Thorn.
The level is the realm-wide minimum: the steppe, forest and Tatar frontiers stay soft throughout.
